<issue identifier="MM-420">
<title>Notify 6/9: wallet Notification Service Extension — decrypt-and-render + unverified notice</title>
<description>
Phase 6 of the <issue id="b95fcd23-95fa-43f6-86a6-81defb9dda77" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-311/e2e-encrypted-notification-relay-for-self-hosted-custos-apns">MM-311</issue> notification relay. Implementation details: `docs/design-plans/2026-07-17-notification-relay-implementation.md`.

## Scope

* **Xcode template:** the forked `scripts/ios/project.yml` (shared by both apps, rendered on every `cargo tauri ios init`) gains an NSE target (`{{app.name}}_NSE`, `type: app-extension`, **Swift-only** — no second Rust staticlib; decryption is CryptoKit, ~200 lines) and `keychain-access-groups` entitlements on both targets. `just ios-template-check` learns the new invariants (NSE target present, entitlements wired) so a template re-render can't silently drop them.
* **NSE behavior:** on `mutable-content: 1` delivery, load the notification private key + pinned sender set from the shared keychain group, HPKE-open (`P256_SHA256_AES_GCM_256`, `authenticatedBy:` the key named by `kid`, `info = "ezpds/notify/1"`), replace placeholder title/body with plaintext.
* **Failure path** (iOS cannot suppress an alert push): unknown `kid`, open failure, or post-reboot locked keychain → render the explicit **unverified notice** ("Couldn't verify a notification from your Custos instance") — never authentic-looking content — and write a diagnostic breadcrumb to a shared app-group container.
* **Diagnostics surface:** the app reads the breadcrumbs and surfaces repeated failures in Settings (key desync / misbehaving relay made visible, per the design doc).
* **Interop check:** on-device XCTest opens the `crates/crypto` golden fixtures with CryptoKit — the cross-implementation verification the fixtures were built for.

## Acceptance

* On-device demo: sealed push from a real Custos renders decrypted content; junk/replayed-junk payload renders the unverified notice; fixture cross-check passes.
* ios-pr-check lane green (template regeneration + postinit + ios-check with the new invariants).
</description>

<title>E2E-encrypted notification relay for self-hosted Custos (APNs)</title>
<description>
Implement the notification relay designed in [docs/design-plans/2026-07-10-notification-relay.md](<https://github.com/malpercio-dev/ezpds/blob/main/docs/design-plans/2026-07-10-notification-relay.md>) (design PR <pull-request id="34230e45-6259-4c9a-b58d-6b135adf84e3" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/review/design-exploration-e2e-encrypted-notification-relay-for-self-hosted-327f880332d1">malpercio-dev/ezpds#207</pull-request>, **merged** — the doc on `main` is the source of truth and incorporates the review hardening: claim-code enrollment authorization for the official relay, versioned sender keys with re-pin/revocation semantics, explicit v1 replay acceptance, unverified-notice rendering for unauthenticated payloads, per-handle APNs topics, serialized-request padding budget, and the post-reboot keychain window).

## Problem

Self-hosted Custos instances need to deliver push notifications to the official iOS apps (Obsign, admin-companion). APNs auth keys are bundle-ID-bound, so self-hosters cannot push directly — a relay is structurally required. The design makes that relay a **blind courier**: trusted for availability only.

## Architecture (see design doc for full detail)

* **Confidentiality:** payloads HPKE-sealed (RFC 9180, DHKEM-P256 + AES-GCM) to a per-device notification key; decrypted on-device by a Notification Service Extension (`mutable-content: 1`). Neither the relay nor Apple sees plaintext.
* **Integrity:** HPKE Auth mode with pinned, versioned per-instance sender keys — the relay cannot forge authenticated content (it can generate detectable junk pushes and replay; v1 accepts duplicates as benign).
* **Metadata minimization:** opaque push handles bound to the instance's iroh node id (no DIDs/handles/raw tokens at the relay), fixed-size padding budgeted against the serialized APNs request, optional content-free ping mode.
* **Transport:** Custos ↔ relay over iroh, new `ezpds/notify/0` ALPN, reusing the persisted node identity (`iroh_identity`) and `iroh_tunnel.rs` patterns; back-channel carries APNs `410 Unregistered` pruning feedback.
* **Sovereignty:** relay is an open-source workspace crate (`crates/notify-relay/`); any instance points at any relay via `[notifications] relay = "<node id>"`. Official relay requires a claim-code enrollment grant; open enrollment is a config option for self-run relays. Caveat: official bundle IDs require the official relay's APNs key.

## Suggested phasing

1. **Relay crate + Custos sender** — `crates/notify-relay/` (claim-code enrollment grants, handle store with per-handle APNs topic, APNs HTTP/2 client, per-node rate limits, serialized-request size validation with 4 KB boundary test) + `[notifications]` config, device notification-key registration route, versioned sender-key set, sealed-send on first trigger (agent claim pending). Loopback iroh e2e tests with mock APNs.
2. **Wallet NSE** — per-device keypair + shared keychain access group, registration in onboarding, decrypt-and-render extension, unverified-notice fallback + in-app diagnostics.
3. **Admin-companion adoption + operator docs** — ops alert triggers, self-relay runbook, metadata-minimizing ping mode.

## Open questions (from the design doc)

* Enrollment grant distribution for the official relay (ceremony mirrors admin-device pairing)
* Replay hardening beyond v1's accept-duplicates posture (per-device counter + durable replay window)
* Delivery receipts over the iroh back-channel (out of scope v1)
* Android/FCM later (envelope is provider-agnostic)

Not yet scheduled into a wave; split into per-phase issues when picked up.
</description>

# Linear Development Workflow

This skill manages the full lifecycle of working on a Linear issue: from picking it up through opening a PR.

## Starting Work on an Issue

When the user indicates they want to work on a Linear issue (e.g., "Let's work on MM-42"):

1. **Parse the issue identifier** from the user's message. The pattern is `MM-` followed by a number.

2. **Fetch the issue details** from Linear using the `get_issue` tool with the parsed identifier. Display a brief summary to the user: title, description (truncated if long), priority, and any existing labels.

3. **Update the issue in Linear:**
   - Set the status to **"In Progress"**
   - Assign it to **"me"** (the authenticated user)

   Use the `save_issue` tool with the issue's `id`, `state: "In Progress"`, and `assignee: "me"`.

4. **Create a git branch from a fresh base** using the issue's suggested branch name:
   - The `get_issue` response includes a `branchName` field — use that as the branch name.
   - **Fetch first, then branch from the remote tip — never from a possibly-stale local HEAD:**
     `git fetch origin main && git checkout -b <branchName> origin/main`
     A stale base silently duplicates work that already merged (hours lost rebuilding an already-shipped backend is the known failure mode).
   - If the branch already exists locally, check it out, then run `git log --oneline <branchName>..origin/main` and surface to the user how far behind the base is.

5. **Verify sibling work is in the base.** If the issue depends on or overlaps sibling issues already marked Done in Linear, confirm their PRs are actually present in the branch base (e.g. `git log --oneline origin/main | grep -i mm-nnn`, or check for the files/routes they added) before concluding any related feature is "missing". **"Linear says Done but the code isn't here" is a hard stop-and-verify signal — it almost always means your base is stale, not that the feature needs building.**

6. **Confirm to the user** what happened: issue assigned, status updated, branch created/checked out (and from which base commit). Then ask what they'd like to tackle first, or summarize the issue so they can dive in.

## Opening a PR (Auto-transition to "In Review")

When the user asks to open a PR, create a pull request, or you detect that a PR is being created for a branch associated with a Linear issue:

1. **Identify the Linear issue** from the current branch name. Linear branch names typically contain the issue identifier (e.g., `malpercio/mm-42-fix-the-thing`). Extract the `MM-XXX` portion.

2. **Create the PR** as the user requests (follow normal PR creation workflow).

3. **After the PR is successfully created**, update the Linear issue:
   - Set the status to **"In Review"**
   - Attach the PR URL as a link on the issue using the `links` field in `save_issue`

   Use `save_issue` with the issue's `id`, `state: "In Review"`, and `links: [{"url": "<pr-url>", "title": "Pull Request"}]`.

4. **Confirm** to the user that the issue has been moved to "In Review" and the PR link has been attached.

## Important Notes

- Always fetch the issue first to confirm it exists and get the full `id` (UUID) needed for updates.
- If the issue is already "In Progress" and assigned, skip those updates and just create the branch.
- If branch creation fails (e.g., uncommitted changes), inform the user and suggest next steps rather than silently failing.
- The PR-to-"In Review" transition should happen automatically whenever a PR is opened during a session where the user started work on a Linear issue. Track the active issue identifier throughout the session.

1	# Notification Relay — Implementation Plan (MM-311)
2	
3	[MM-311](https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-311) · implementation leg of
4	[docs/design-plans/2026-07-10-notification-relay.md](2026-07-10-notification-relay.md)
5	(design PR #207, merged — that doc remains the architecture source of truth; this doc pins
6	the implementation details against the codebase and decomposes the work into issues).
7	
8	**Codebase verified: 2026-07-17** (migrations at V051, bruno seq at 123, iroh 1.0.0,
9	workspace 0.5.2).
10	
11	## Refinements to the design doc
12	
13	Three details discovered during codebase verification refine (not reverse) the design:
14	
15	1. **Registrations key on the account DID, not `devices.id`.** The design says the
16	   registration lands in "new columns/table beside `devices`" — but `devices` is a
17	   *transient pre-DID artifact*: rows are deleted inside the DID-promotion transaction
18	   (`routes/create_did.rs`) and the table FKs to `pending_accounts`. A registration FK'd
19	   there would die exactly when the account starts mattering. Wallet notification
20	   registrations therefore key on `(did, device_uuid)` where `device_uuid` is an
21	   app-generated stable identifier, are created **post-promotion** over the OAuth/DPoP
22	   channel (through the `authenticate_access` seam — the auth-seam-check applies), and are
23	   purged in `account_delete::purge_account`'s explicit FK-ordered delete list.
24	   Admin-companion registrations are a separate table keyed by `admin_devices.id`,
25	   cleaned up alongside the revoke tombstone. Pending (pre-DID) accounts get no pushes —
26	   onboarding completes with promotion, and registration is one of the first
27	   post-promotion calls.
28	2. **The ciphersuite is forced to AES-256-GCM.** CryptoKit ships exactly one P-256 HPKE
29	   suite: `HPKE.Ciphersuite.P256_SHA256_AES_GCM_256`. So the wire suite is pinned to
30	   **DHKEM(P-256, HKDF-SHA256) + HKDF-SHA256 + AES-256-GCM, mode_auth** — no
31	   negotiation, ever; `v` in the envelope names the whole suite. RFC 9180's appendix has
32	   no test vector for this exact combo (A.3 is AES-128), so golden fixtures are generated
33	   from the Rust implementation, pinned in `crates/crypto/tests/fixtures/`, and
34	   cross-verified against CryptoKit by an on-device XCTest in the wallet phase.
35	3. **The v1 back-channel is the RPC response, not a server-initiated stream.** The relay
36	   calls APNs synchronously inside the push RPC, so `410 Unregistered` (and throttle/size
37	   outcomes) return in the same request/response exchange over the already-open bidi
38	   stream. No relay-initiated streams in v1 — that machinery (delivery receipts) stays
39	   out of scope, as the design already decided.
40	
41	CryptoKit's HPKE API requires **iOS 17**; the apps' deployment target currently rides
42	tauri-cli's default (13.0, nothing overridden in either `tauri.conf.json`). Decision:
43	raise `bundle > iOS > minimumSystemVersion` to `17.0` for both apps in the wallet phase.
44	Both apps are new (no installed base below 17), and a per-target split (NSE at 17, app
45	lower, runtime-gated registration) buys nothing but complexity.
46	
47	## Wire formats
48	
49	### Sealed payload (Custos → device, opaque to relay/Apple)
50	
51	Plaintext (serde_json, camelCase):
52	
53	```json
54	{ "type": "agent_claim_pending", "title": "…", "body": "…", "data": { … }, "pad": "…" }
55	```
56	
57	`pad` is a string of `0x20` bytes sized so the **serialized APNs request** lands exactly
58	on a padding bucket (below). Sealed with HPKE mode_auth:
59	
60	- suite: DHKEM(P-256, HKDF-SHA256), HKDF-SHA256, AES-256-GCM
61	- `info = b"ezpds/notify/1"`, `aad = b""` (version binding lives in `info` + envelope `v`)
62	- sender key: the instance's static notification sender keypair named by `kid`
63	- recipient key: the device's notification public key
64	
65	### APNs payload (relay → Apple → device)
66	
67	```json
68	{
69	  "aps": { "alert": { "title": "Custos", "body": "Encrypted notification" },
70	           "mutable-content": 1 },
71	  "ezpds": { "v": 1, "kid": 3, "enc": "<b64url encapsulated key>", "ct": "<b64url ciphertext>" }
72	}
73	```
74	
75	Ping mode (later phase) replaces `aps` with `{ "content-available": 1 }` and omits
76	`ezpds` entirely.
77	
78	### Padding buckets
79	
80	Buckets are defined on the **serialized APNs JSON body**: `{1024, 2048, 3584}` bytes
81	(3584 keeps headroom under APNs' 4096 cap). Base64url expansion is deterministic
82	(`enc` = 65-byte uncompressed P-256 point → 87 chars; `ct` = plaintext + 16-byte tag),
83	so Custos computes the exact `pad` length that makes the final body hit the smallest
84	bucket ≥ the unpadded size, and refuses payloads that exceed the largest bucket. A
85	relay-side check enforces the same cap defensively, with a boundary test at exactly
86	4096 bytes.
87	
88	### Custos ↔ relay RPC (`ezpds/notify/0`)
89	
90	New ALPN beside `ezpds/iroh/0`. One JSON request per bidi stream, response JSON, stream
91	FIN delimits (the `iroh_tunnel.rs` pattern: `read_to_end` with a 64 KiB cap, 30 s
92	per-stream timeout). The dialing node's identity is `connection.remote_id()` — no
93	credential in the messages. Requests are a tagged enum:
94	
95	| request | response | notes |
96	|---|---|---|
97	| `enroll { claimCode? }` | `ok` / `denied` | idempotent; `claimCode` required unless the relay runs open enrollment |
98	| `registerHandle { apnsToken, apnsTopic }` | `{ handle }` | topic must be in the relay's served-topic set; re-registering the same token rotates the handle |
99	| `dropHandle { handle }` | `ok` | idempotent |
100	| `push { handle, kid, enc, ct, priority, ttlSecs, ping }` | `{ outcome }` | outcome ∈ `delivered · unregistered · throttled · tooLarge · notEnrolled · unknownHandle · apnsError` |

    The device half of the encrypted notification relay MM-418 landed the server
    side of. Obsign generates a per-device P-256 notification key, registers it with
    each identity's Custos, and re-pins the sender keys that instance publishes.
    
    Three things are worth reviewing carefully.
    
    **The keychain surface is an accessibility class, not a new store.** The shared
    access group already exists — `org.obsign.shared` is first in the entitlement
    array, so every item already lands somewhere a Notification Service Extension
    can reach. What the extension additionally needs is
    `kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlock`, because a push arrives on a locked screen.
    `store_item_after_first_unlock` writes into the *same* device-local store as
    `store_item` and is read by the same `get_item`; the write is delete-then-add
    because `SecItemUpdate` cannot change an existing item's protection class, and
    the class is the whole contract. The class is confined to notification material:
    it opens content, signs nothing, and is on the never-sync deny list.
    
    **The pinned sender-key set is keyed by hosting server.** `kid` is an
    autoincrement column on one instance, and two instances will both publish a
    `kid` of 1 for unrelated keys — which this wallet, holding identities on
    several hosts, would silently collapse into one entry. The extension will try
    every candidate under an incoming `kid`; HPKE Auth mode fails closed on a wrong
    sender key, so trying costs nothing.
    
    **A successful fetch replaces a host's set wholesale.** That single choice is
    what implements the design's rotation semantics: a key the operator revokes
    disappears from the device at its next contact. Merging would keep a compromised
    key pinned forever, which is the window re-pin-on-every-contact exists to close.
    A 501 or 503 changes nothing — neither is a revocation, and clearing on one
    would strip every device that checked in during a bad deploy.
    
    The APNs bridge is iOS-only and adds the two device-token delegate methods to
    Tauri's delegate class rather than swizzling: `class_addMethod` fails if the
    selector already exists, and declining is the outcome we want if Tauri ever
    implements them itself. Everything with logic worth testing lives in
    `notifications.rs` instead, since the bridge is only ever compiled by the
    cross-compile lane and only ever exercised on a device.
    
    Both apps move to iOS 17, where CryptoKit's HPKE API begins.
    
    Registration reports "no APNs token yet" and "this host runs no relay" as
    outcomes rather than errors, so the onboarding-completion call has nothing to
    catch on a simulator or for an identity hosted on a standard PDS.
    
    Not verified without a device: the delegate installation, the permission prompt,
    and that a real token round-trips. The iOS cross-compile is the only automated
    check those paths get.

1	// pattern: Mixed (Functional Core pin-store arithmetic; Imperative Shell commands + Keychain)
2	//
3	// The device half of the end-to-end-encrypted notification relay: the keys a Custos instance
4	// seals push payloads to, the registration that tells it where to send them, and the pinned
5	// sender-key set the Notification Service Extension verifies against.
6	//
7	//   register_for_notifications(did)         — POST /v1/notifications/register
8	//   refresh_notification_sender_keys(did)   — GET  /v1/notifications/sender-keys (the re-pin)
9	//   get_notification_diagnostics()          — what this device holds, for Settings
10	//
11	// Nothing here decrypts anything. The extension that does is a separate target (a later phase);
12	// this module's whole job is to leave the right material in the right Keychain slots under the
13	// right protection class, and to keep the pinned set fresh.
14	//
15	// # Why the material is device-global rather than per-DID
16	//
17	// A push arrives at the extension as `{v, kid, enc, ct}` and nothing else — no DID, no handle,
18	// no account hint, because naming one would hand the relay and Apple the metadata the whole
19	// design exists to withhold. So the recipient key cannot be per-identity: the extension would
20	// have no way to choose among several. One device, one notification keypair, one `device_uuid`;
21	// every identity on the device registers the same public key with its own host.
22	//
23	// # Why the pinned set is per-host anyway
24	//
25	// `kid` is an autoincrement column on *one* Custos instance. Two instances will both publish a
26	// `kid` of 1 for entirely unrelated keys, and this wallet routinely holds identities on more
27	// than one. So the pin store is a map from hosting server to that server's published set, and
28	// the extension tries every candidate key registered under the incoming `kid`. That costs
29	// nothing and cannot go wrong: HPKE Auth mode either authenticates against a given sender key
30	// or it does not, so a wrong candidate fails closed and the next is tried. A single flat set
31	// keyed by `kid` alone would instead have two instances silently overwriting each other.
32	//
33	// # Re-pinning is wholesale replacement
34	//
35	// A successful fetch replaces that host's entry entirely rather than merging into it. That one
36	// choice is what implements all three rotation semantics from the design: a new key appears, a
37	// retired key stays as long as the server keeps publishing it, and a *revoked* key vanishes from
38	// this device the first time it contacts its Custos. Merging would keep a compromised key
39	// pinned forever, which is precisely the window re-pin-on-every-contact exists to close.
40	//
41	// A failed fetch changes nothing. An instance that answers 501 has not revoked anything — it has
42	// switched the feature off, or was never configured — and a 503 means it could not read its own
43	// keys. Treating either as "revoke everything" would let one bad deploy strip the pins off every
44	// device that happened to check in during it.

410	            .filter(|t| !t.is_empty()),
411	        Err(e) if crate::keychain::is_not_found(&e) => None,
412	        Err(e) => {
413	            tracing::warn!(error = %e, "could not read the stored APNs token");
414	            None
415	        }
416	    }

429	/// The pin store as it currently stands. Never fails: an unreadable document reads as empty
430	/// (see [`PinnedSenderKeys`]).
431	fn load_pins() -> PinnedSenderKeys {
432	    let raw = match crate::keychain::get_item(PINNED_SENDER_KEYS_ACCOUNT) {
433	        Ok(bytes) => bytes,
434	        Err(e) => {
435	            if !crate::keychain::is_not_found(&e) {
436	                tracing::warn!(error = %e, "could not read pinned sender keys; treating as empty");
437	            }
438	            return PinnedSenderKeys {
439	                version: PIN_DOCUMENT_VERSION,
440	                hosts: BTreeMap::new(),
441	            };
442	        }
443	    };
444	    match serde_json::from_slice::<PinnedSenderKeys>(&raw) {
445	        Ok(pins) if pins.version == PIN_DOCUMENT_VERSION => pins,
446	        Ok(pins) => {
447	            tracing::warn!(
448	                version = pins.version,
449	                "pinned sender keys were written by a different build; re-pinning from scratch"
450	            );
451	            PinnedSenderKeys {
452	                version: PIN_DOCUMENT_VERSION,
453	                hosts: BTreeMap::new(),
454	            }
455	        }
456	        Err(e) => {
457	            tracing::warn!(error = %e, "pinned sender keys are corrupt; re-pinning from scratch");
458	            PinnedSenderKeys {
459	                version: PIN_DOCUMENT_VERSION,
460	                hosts: BTreeMap::new(),
461	            }
462	        }
463	    }
464	}

466	/// Replace one host's pinned set, leaving every other host untouched.
467	///
468	/// Wholesale for the named host — that is the revocation mechanism — and surgical across hosts,
469	/// because a contact with one identity's Custos says nothing about another's.
470	/// One shared document means one writer at a time.
471	///
472	/// `+page.svelte` fires a registration per identity **without awaiting**, and each one re-pins on
473	/// the same contact, so two of these read-modify-writes genuinely overlap on Tauri's multi-thread
474	/// runtime. Losing the later write is not merely a stale entry: if the discarded pass was the
475	/// contact that dropped a *revoked* sender key, that host keeps trusting the revoked key until
476	/// its next contact — reopening the exact window the module header says re-pinning closes.
477	///
478	/// A `std::sync::Mutex` deliberately: the guard is taken and released entirely inside this
479	/// synchronous function and never crosses an `.await`.
480	static PIN_WRITE_LOCK: std::sync::Mutex<()> = std::sync::Mutex::new(());
481	
482	fn store_pins_for_host(host: &str, keys: &[SenderKey]) -> Result<(), NotificationsError> {
483	    // A poisoned lock means some other thread panicked mid-write; the document is re-read below
484	    // either way, so recovering is strictly better than propagating the panic into a re-pin.
485	    let _guard = PIN_WRITE_LOCK.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
486	    let mut pins = load_pins();
487	    pins.version = PIN_DOCUMENT_VERSION;
488	    pins.hosts.insert(host.to_string(), keys.to_vec());
489	
490	    let encoded = serde_json::to_vec(&pins).map_err(|e| NotificationsError::KeychainError {
491	        message: format!("could not encode pinned sender keys: {e}"),
492	    })?;
493	    crate::keychain::store_item_after_first_unlock(PINNED_SENDER_KEYS_ACCOUNT, &encoded)
494	        .map_err(keychain_err)
495	}

499	fn oauth_err(e: crate::oauth::OAuthError) -> NotificationsError {
500	    NotificationsError::NetworkError {
501	        message: e.to_string(),
502	    }
503	}
504	
505	/// `POST /v1/notifications/register`. `Ok(false)` is the host's 501 — it serves no notification
506	/// routes — which the caller reports as `Unsupported` rather than an error.
507	async fn register_impl(
508	    client: &OAuthClient,
509	    request: &RegisterRequest<'_>,
510	) -> Result<bool, NotificationsError> {
511	    let resp = client
512	        .post("/v1/notifications/register", request)
513	        .await
514	        .map_err(oauth_err)?;
515	    match resp.status().as_u16() {
516	        200 => Ok(true),
517	        501 => Ok(false),
518	        429 => Err(NotificationsError::RateLimited {
519	            retry_after: resp
520	                .headers()
521	                .get("retry-after")
522	                .and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok())
523	                .map(str::to_string),
524	        }),
525	        other => Err(NotificationsError::ServerError {
526	            status: Some(other),
527	            message: server_message(resp, "registration was refused").await,
528	        }),
529	    }
530	}

532	/// `GET /v1/notifications/sender-keys`. `Ok(None)` is the 501; every other non-200 is an error,
533	/// including the 503 an instance returns when it cannot read its own keys — pinning nothing on
534	/// that basis would leave the device silently unable to verify anything it later receives.
535	async fn fetch_sender_keys_impl(
536	    client: &OAuthClient,
537	) -> Result<Option<Vec<SenderKey>>, NotificationsError> {
538	    let resp = client
539	        .get("/v1/notifications/sender-keys")
540	        .await
541	        .map_err(oauth_err)?;
542	    match resp.status().as_u16() {
543	        200 => {
544	            let body: SenderKeysResponse =
545	                resp.json()
546	                    .await
547	                    .map_err(|e| NotificationsError::ServerError {
548	                        status: Some(200),
549	                        message: format!("could not parse the sender-key set: {e}"),
550	                    })?;
551	            Ok(Some(body.keys))
552	        }
553	        501 => Ok(None),
554	        429 => Err(NotificationsError::RateLimited {
555	            retry_after: resp
556	                .headers()
557	                .get("retry-after")
558	                .and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok())
559	                .map(str::to_string),
560	        }),
561	        other => Err(NotificationsError::ServerError {
562	            status: Some(other),
563	            message: server_message(resp, "the sender-key set is unavailable").await,
564	        }),
565	    }
566	}

568	/// The server's own error message where it sent one, so the screen shows the real reason instead
569	/// of a status code.
570	async fn server_message(resp: reqwest::Response, fallback: &str) -> String {
571	    #[derive(Deserialize)]
572	    struct Envelope {
573	        error: Option<Inner>,
574	    }
575	    #[derive(Deserialize)]
576	    struct Inner {
577	        message: Option<String>,
578	    }
579	    resp.json::<Envelope>()
580	        .await
581	        .ok()
582	        .and_then(|e| e.error)
583	        .and_then(|e| e.message)
584	        .unwrap_or_else(|| fallback.to_string())
585	}

587	/// Resolve the DID's full-access session (restore / refresh, or `SessionLocked`).
588	async fn full_access_session(
589	    pds_client: &PdsClient,
590	    did: &str,
591	) -> Result<crate::session_provider::ActiveSession, NotificationsError> {
592	    // Not `NetworkError`: an unreadable clock is a local fault, and this module's rule is that
593	    // only a transport failure may be reported as one — otherwise the screen offers connectivity
594	    // advice for a problem connectivity cannot fix.
595	    let now = crate::sovereign_session::unix_timestamp().map_err(|_| {
596	        NotificationsError::ServerError {
597	            status: None,
598	            message: "system clock is unavailable".to_string(),
599	        }
600	    })?;
601	    SessionProvider
602	        .full_access_client(pds_client, &IdentityStore, did, now)
603	        .await
604	        .map_err(map_session_error)
605	}

609	/// Tauri command: register this device for push on the identity's hosting Custos.
610	///
611	/// Called at onboarding completion (post-promotion, so the account exists and can be
612	/// authenticated) and again whenever the APNs token changes. Idempotent on the server, which
613	/// upserts on `(did, device_uuid)`, so a repeat is free — which is what lets the caller fire it
614	/// without tracking whether it already has.
615	#[tauri::command]
616	pub async fn register_for_notifications(
617	    app: tauri::AppHandle,
618	    state: tauri::State<'_, crate::oauth::AppState>,
619	    did: String,
620	) -> Result<RegistrationOutcome, NotificationsError> {
621	    // The topic is the app's own bundle identifier, read from the running configuration rather
622	    // than restated as a constant here — APNs routes on the identifier the binary was actually
623	    // built with, and a rename that missed a hardcoded copy would fail at the relay, one hop
624	    // away from anything that could explain it.
625	    register_identity(&app.config().identifier, state.pds_client(), &did).await
626	}

628	/// Register one identity, given the APNs topic and a PDS client.
629	///
630	/// Split out from the command because the APNs token-change callback re-registers every managed
631	/// identity from a context that has no Tauri `State` — and a second implementation of the same
632	/// sequence is exactly how the two would drift.
633	pub(crate) async fn register_identity(
634	    apns_topic: &str,
635	    pds_client: &PdsClient,
636	    did: &str,
637	) -> Result<RegistrationOutcome, NotificationsError> {
638	    let device_uuid = device_uuid()?;
639	
640	    // Checked before the key is generated or the session resolved: with no token there is
641	    // nothing to register, and minting key material for a registration that cannot happen would
642	    // pin this device to a key its host has never heard of.
643	    let Some(apns_token) = stored_apns_token() else {
644	        return Ok(RegistrationOutcome {
645	            status: RegistrationStatus::AwaitingApnsToken,
646	            device_uuid,
647	            notification_key_id: None,
648	        });
649	    };
650	
651	    let notification_key_id = load_or_create_notification_key()?;
652	    let session = full_access_session(pds_client, did).await?;
653	
654	    let registered = register_impl(
655	        &session.client,
656	        &RegisterRequest {
657	            device_uuid: &device_uuid,
658	            notification_public_key: &notification_key_id,
659	            apns_token: &apns_token,
660	            apns_topic,
661	        },
662	    )
663	    .await?;
664	
665	    // The same contact re-pins. The registration is the first moment this device could receive
666	    // anything from this host, so it is also the first moment it needs the keys to verify it.
667	    if registered {
668	        if let Err(e) = pin_sender_keys(&session.client, &session.pds_url).await {
669	            tracing::warn!(error = ?e, "registered for push but could not pin sender keys");
670	        }
671	    }
672	
673	    Ok(RegistrationOutcome {
674	        status: if registered {
675	            RegistrationStatus::Registered
676	        } else {
677	            RegistrationStatus::Unsupported
678	        },
679	        device_uuid,
680	        notification_key_id: Some(notification_key_id),
681	    })
682	}

684	/// Re-register every managed identity, after the APNs token changed under us.
685	///
686	/// Per identity rather than once: the registration lives on each identity's own hosting Custos,
687	/// which may be a different server (or no Custos at all). Failures are logged and stepped over —
688	/// one identity whose host is unreachable must not cost the others their new token, and the next
689	/// contact retries anyway.
690	#[cfg(target_os = "ios")]
691	pub(crate) async fn re_register_every_identity(apns_topic: &str, pds_client: &PdsClient) {
692	    let dids = match IdentityStore.list_identities() {
693	        Ok(dids) => dids,
694	        Err(e) => {
695	            tracing::warn!(error = ?e, "could not list identities to re-register for push");
696	            return;
697	        }
698	    };
699	    for did in dids {
700	        match register_identity(apns_topic, pds_client, &did).await {
701	            Ok(outcome) => {
702	                tracing::info!(did = %did, status = ?outcome.status, "re-registered for push")
703	            }
704	            Err(e) => tracing::warn!(did = %did, error = ?e, "could not re-register for push"),
705	        }
706	    }
707	}

709	/// Tauri command: re-fetch and re-pin the identity's host's sender-key set.
710	///
711	/// The frontend calls this on every successful contact with a Custos. That cadence is the
712	/// design's compromise-window property, not housekeeping: a sender key the operator revokes
713	/// stops being trusted on this device at the next contact, and nothing shorter than that is
714	/// available without a channel the relay could interfere with.
715	#[tauri::command]
716	pub async fn refresh_notification_sender_keys(
717	    state: tauri::State<'_, crate::oauth::AppState>,
718	    did: String,
719	) -> Result<SenderKeyPinning, NotificationsError> {
720	    let session = full_access_session(state.pds_client(), &did).await?;
721	    pin_sender_keys(&session.client, &session.pds_url).await
722	}
723	
724	/// Fetch and store one host's set. Shared by the re-pin command and the registration path.
725	async fn pin_sender_keys(
726	    client: &OAuthClient,
727	    pds_url: &str,
728	) -> Result<SenderKeyPinning, NotificationsError> {
729	    let host = host_key(pds_url);
730	    match fetch_sender_keys_impl(client).await? {
731	        Some(keys) => {
732	            store_pins_for_host(&host, &keys)?;
733	            Ok(SenderKeyPinning {
734	                host,
735	                pinned: true,
736	                keys,
737	            })
738	        }
739	        None => {
740	            let keys = load_pins().hosts.get(&host).cloned().unwrap_or_default();
741	            Ok(SenderKeyPinning {
742	                host,
743	                pinned: false,
744	                keys,
745	            })
746	        }
747	    }
748	}

1141	    /// A Bearer client pointed at the mock server, carrying a far-future access token so no
1142	    /// refresh fires ahead of the request under test (the `agents.rs` test-client shape).
1143	    fn mock_client(base_url: &str) -> OAuthClient {
1144	        use base64::engine::general_purpose::URL_SAFE_NO_PAD;
1145	        use base64::Engine;
1146	
1147	        let exp = std::time::SystemTime::now()
1148	            .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
1149	            .unwrap()
1150	            .as_secs()
1151	            + 3600;
1152	        let header = URL_SAFE_NO_PAD.encode(r#"{"alg":"ES256"}"#);
1153	        let payload = URL_SAFE_NO_PAD.encode(format!(r#"{{"exp":{exp}}}"#).as_bytes());
1154	
1155	        OAuthClient::new_bearer(
1156	            format!("{header}.{payload}.sig"),
1157	            "refresh".to_string(),
1158	            base_url.to_string(),
1159	        )
1160	        .expect("new_bearer must succeed")
1161	    }

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# ios-check.sh — fail (non-zero) if the gitignored Xcode project is missing any of
3	# the required workarounds. Run before an iOS build, or in CI.
4	#
5	# The workarounds are no longer patched into the generated project by script — they
6	# come from the committed XcodeGen template scripts/ios/project.yml, rendered by
7	# `cargo tauri ios init` (via `bundle > iOS > template` in tauri.conf.json). This
8	# checker verifies the END STATE of the generated project, so it catches every way
9	# the template can fail to apply: a dropped `template` config key, a tauri-cli
10	# behavior change, or a stale gen/apple from before the template era. On failure,
11	# the fix is always: re-run `cargo tauri ios init` (from apps/<app>) then
12	# `just <recipe>-postinit`.
13	#
14	# SINGLE shared implementation for both app lanes; each app keeps a thin wrapper at
15	# apps/<app>/scripts/ios-check.sh that pins its app dir and recipe prefix. The
16	# framework list is read from the app's tauri.conf.json (bundle > iOS > frameworks)
17	# — the same source the template renders OTHER_LDFLAGS from — so there is no second
18	# copy to drift.
19	#
20	# Usage: ios-check.sh <app-dir> <recipe-prefix>
21	set -euo pipefail
22	
23	if [ "$#" -ne 2 ]; then
24	  echo "usage: $(basename "$0") <app-dir> <recipe-prefix>" >&2
25	  exit 2
26	fi
27	APP_DIR="$(cd "$1" && pwd)"
28	RECIPE="$2"
29	
30	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
31	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "${SCRIPT_DIR}/../.." && pwd)"
32	REINIT_HINT="(re-run 'cargo tauri ios init' from ${APP_DIR}, then 'just ${RECIPE}-postinit')"
33	
34	# shellcheck source=scripts/ios/lib.sh
35	. "${SCRIPT_DIR}/lib.sh"
36	
37	PBXPROJ="$(ls "${APP_DIR}"/src-tauri/gen/apple/*.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)"
38	if [ -z "${PBXPROJ}" ]; then
39	  echo "ios-check: FAIL — no project.pbxproj (run 'cargo tauri ios init' then 'just ${RECIPE}-postinit')" >&2
40	  exit 1
41	fi
42	
43	fail=0
44	
45	# Patch A: the swift-rs fork must be declared in Cargo.toml AND applied in Cargo.lock.
46	if ! "${REPO_ROOT}/scripts/swift-rs-patch-check.sh"; then
47	  echo "ios-check: FAIL — swift-rs [patch.crates-io] override missing or not applied (see above)" >&2
48	  fail=1
49	fi
50	
51	# The generated project.yml must come from OUR template (its header carries the
52	# sentinel comment). A stock project.yml means `bundle > iOS > template` did not
53	# apply — none of the workarounds below can be trusted to be present.
54	PROJYML="$(dirname "${PBXPROJ}")/../project.yml"
55	if [ ! -f "${PROJYML}" ] || ! grep -q 'ezpds-ios-template' "${PROJYML}"; then
56	  echo "ios-check: FAIL — gen/apple/project.yml not rendered from scripts/ios/project.yml; check bundle > iOS > template in tauri.conf.json ${REINIT_HINT}" >&2
57	  fail=1
58	fi
59	
60	# macOS 26's Run Script sandbox blocks Cargo's readdir (docs/ios-upstream-bugs.md
61	# Bug 2). The template forces the setting off; require the explicit NO (a missing
62	# setting would fall back to Xcode's default, which is YES on Xcode 14+).
63	if ! grep -q 'ENABLE_USER_SCRIPT_SANDBOXING = NO' "${PBXPROJ}" || grep -q 'ENABLE_USER_SCRIPT_SANDBOXING = YES' "${PBXPROJ}"; then
64	  echo "ios-check: FAIL — ENABLE_USER_SCRIPT_SANDBOXING is not forced to NO ${REINIT_HINT}" >&2
65	  fail=1
66	fi
67	
68	# The Build Rust Code phase must carry the dev-env preamble from the template —
69	# Xcode runs it in a clean shell that inherits neither the devenv PATH nor the
70	# ios-env.sh toolchain overrides.
71	if ! grep -q '# >>> ezpds-ios-env >>>' "${PBXPROJ}"; then
72	  echo "ios-check: FAIL — Build Rust Code phase missing the ezpds-ios-env preamble ${REINIT_HINT}" >&2
73	  fail=1
74	fi
75	
76	# Tolerates Xcode's spurious "entitlements modified during build" caused by the
77	# per-build project restamp (docs/ios-upstream-bugs.md Bug 3).
78	if ! grep -q 'CODE_SIGN_ALLOW_ENTITLEMENTS_MODIFICATION = YES' "${PBXPROJ}"; then
79	  echo "ios-check: FAIL — CODE_SIGN_ALLOW_ENTITLEMENTS_MODIFICATION missing ${REINIT_HINT}" >&2
80	  fail=1
81	fi
82	
83	# Entitlements: tauri's DEFAULT path in the project + Patch H content injection.
84	# tauri-cli's build-time codesign reads gen/apple/<name>_iOS/<name>_iOS.entitlements
85	# regardless of what project.yml says, so (a) CODE_SIGN_ENTITLEMENTS must point at
86	# that default — a repoint leaves it fileless and signing dies with "cannot read
87	# entitlement data" — and (b) postinit's Patch H must have overwritten that generated
88	# file with the tracked source of truth (so the wallet's iCloud grants actually reach
89	# the signed app), verified by a plist lint + the sha marker.
90	TRACKED_ENT="${APP_DIR}/src-tauri/Entitlements.ios.plist"
91	if [ ! -f "${TRACKED_ENT}" ]; then
92	  echo "ios-check: FAIL — ${TRACKED_ENT} missing (the entitlements source of truth)" >&2
93	  fail=1
94	fi
95	if ! grep -qE 'CODE_SIGN_ENTITLEMENTS = "?[^"/;]+_iOS/[^"/;]+_iOS\.entitlements"?;' "${PBXPROJ}"; then
96	  echo "ios-check: FAIL — CODE_SIGN_ENTITLEMENTS is not tauri's default <name>_iOS/<name>_iOS.entitlements path; a repoint breaks tauri's build-time codesign ${REINIT_HINT}" >&2
97	  fail=1
98	fi
99	IOS_SRC_DIR="$(ios_src_dir "${PBXPROJ}")"
100	if [ -z "${IOS_SRC_DIR}" ]; then
101	  echo "ios-check: FAIL — no <name>_iOS source dir under gen/apple/ to hold entitlements ${REINIT_HINT}" >&2
102	  fail=1
103	elif [ -f "${TRACKED_ENT}" ]; then
104	  ENT_FILE="${IOS_SRC_DIR}/$(basename "${IOS_SRC_DIR}").entitlements"
105	  ENT_MARKER="${IOS_SRC_DIR}/.ezpds-entitlements.sha256"
106	  if [ ! -f "${ENT_FILE}" ]; then
107	    echo "ios-check: FAIL — generated entitlements ${ENT_FILE} missing; tauri's codesign will fail to read it ${REINIT_HINT}" >&2
108	    fail=1
109	  elif command -v plutil >/dev/null 2>&1 && ! plutil -lint "${ENT_FILE}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
110	    echo "ios-check: FAIL — generated entitlements ${ENT_FILE} is not a valid plist (codesign 'cannot read entitlement data') ${REINIT_HINT}" >&2
111	    fail=1
112	  elif [ ! -f "${ENT_MARKER}" ] || [ "$(cat "${ENT_MARKER}")" != "$(sha256_file "${TRACKED_ENT}")" ]; then
113	    echo "ios-check: FAIL — generated entitlements not installed from ${TRACKED_ENT} (run 'just ${RECIPE}-postinit' — Patch H) ${REINIT_HINT}" >&2
114	    fail=1
115	  fi
116	fi
117	
118	# Every Apple framework the Rust staticlib needs (bundle > iOS > frameworks in
119	# tauri.conf.json) must be linked on ONE shared OTHER_LDFLAGS line. A bare-string
120	# grep is insufficient: a split or duplicated OTHER_LDFLAGS (two assignments for
121	# the same build config) would still contain every name while the later one SHADOWS
122	# the earlier, silently dropping a framework. So validate the EFFECTIVE state: at
123	# least one OTHER_LDFLAGS line links all of them (in tauri.conf.json order, which is
124	# the order the template renders), and NO OTHER_LDFLAGS line links only a subset.
125	# (`|| true`: grep -c exits 1 on zero matches, which would trip `set -e`.)
126	CONF="${APP_DIR}/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json"
127	# python3 ships with Xcode's CLT (dev Macs) and the GitHub macOS runners.
128	# `read -a` (not mapfile: absent from the bash 3.2 on dev Macs) splits the
129	# space-separated names without the glob expansion an unquoted $() would risk.
130	IFS=' ' read -r -a FRAMEWORKS <<< "$(python3 -c "
131	import json
132	conf = json.load(open('${CONF}'))
133	print(' '.join(conf.get('bundle', {}).get('iOS', {}).get('frameworks', [])))
134	")"
135	if [ "${#FRAMEWORKS[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
136	  echo "ios-check: FAIL — no bundle > iOS > frameworks in ${CONF} (SystemConfiguration is required by the system-configuration crate)" >&2
137	  fail=1
138	else
139	  canon_re="OTHER_LDFLAGS = "
140	  for fw in "${FRAMEWORKS[@]}"; do
141	    canon_re="${canon_re}.*-framework ${fw}"
142	  done
143	  ldflags_all=$(grep -cE "${canon_re}" "${PBXPROJ}" || true)
144	  if [ "${ldflags_all}" -lt 1 ]; then
145	    echo "ios-check: FAIL — no OTHER_LDFLAGS line links all of: ${FRAMEWORKS[*]} ${REINIT_HINT}" >&2
146	    fail=1
147	  else
148	    for fw in "${FRAMEWORKS[@]}"; do
149	      ldflags_fw=$(grep -cE "OTHER_LDFLAGS = .*-framework ${fw}" "${PBXPROJ}" || true)
150	      if [ "${ldflags_fw}" -ne "${ldflags_all}" ]; then
151	        echo "ios-check: FAIL — a partial/split OTHER_LDFLAGS links ${fw} separately; a shadowed assignment drops frameworks ${REINIT_HINT}" >&2
152	        fail=1
153	      fi
154	    done
155	  fi
156	fi
157	
158	# The Rust staticlib must NOT be copied into the bundle — App Store upload rejects a
159	# standalone `libapp.a` ("Invalid bundle structure", tauri#13578). The template
160	# excludes it at the source (Externals -> buildPhase: none); verify both layers.
161	if grep -q 'libapp\.a in Resources' "${PBXPROJ}"; then
162	  echo "ios-check: FAIL — libapp.a still in Copy Bundle Resources, pbxproj ${REINIT_HINT}" >&2
163	  fail=1
164	fi
165	if [ -f "${PROJYML}" ] && grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*path:[[:space:]]*Externals[[:space:]]*$' "${PROJYML}" \
166	   && ! grep -A1 -E '^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*path:[[:space:]]*Externals[[:space:]]*$' "${PROJYML}" | grep -q 'buildPhase: none'; then
167	  echo "ios-check: FAIL — project.yml Externals lacks 'buildPhase: none'; libapp.a would be re-bundled ${REINIT_HINT}" >&2
168	  fail=1
169	fi
170	
171	# Patch G: when the app ships a brand icon (apps/<app>/app-icon.png), the regenerated
172	# asset catalog must have been built from exactly that file — postinit stamps its
173	# sha256 into the catalog (resampled PNGs can't be byte-compared to the source).
174	if [ -f "${APP_DIR}/app-icon.png" ]; then
175	  # sha256_file: from lib.sh (sourced above) — the same hasher ios-postinit stamps with.
176	  marker="$(dirname "${PBXPROJ}")/../Assets.xcassets/AppIcon.appiconset/.ezpds-app-icon.sha256"
177	  if [ ! -f "${marker}" ] || [ "$(cat "${marker}")" != "$(sha256_file "${APP_DIR}/app-icon.png")" ]; then
178	    echo "ios-check: FAIL — AppIcon.appiconset not regenerated from app-icon.png (run 'just ${RECIPE}-postinit')" >&2
179	    fail=1
180	  fi
181	fi
182	
183	# The layered Icon Composer document (apps/<app>/AppIcon.icon, the iOS 26 Liquid
184	# Glass icon) must be registered by the template: referenced in place in project.yml
185	# (with the fileTypes .icon=file mapping, else XcodeGen explodes the package into
186	# loose resources — XcodeGen#1556) and linked into the pbxproj Resources phase.
187	# Two pbxproj occurrences required: the PBXBuildFile definition AND the
188	# Resources-phase files entry both carry the "AppIcon.icon in Resources" comment —
189	# a bare -q would be satisfied by the definition alone.
190	if [ -d "${APP_DIR}/AppIcon.icon" ]; then
191	  if [ -f "${PROJYML}" ]; then
192	    if ! grep -A2 -E '^[[:space:]]*fileTypes:' "${PROJYML}" | grep -q 'icon:' \
193	       || ! grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*path:[[:space:]]*\.\./\.\./\.\./AppIcon\.icon[[:space:]]*$' "${PROJYML}"; then
194	      echo "ios-check: FAIL — project.yml missing the AppIcon.icon resource or the fileTypes .icon=file mapping ${REINIT_HINT}" >&2
195	      fail=1
196	    fi
197	  fi
198	  icon_res_count=$(grep -c 'AppIcon\.icon in Resources' "${PBXPROJ}" || true)
199	  if [ "${icon_res_count}" -lt 2 ]; then
200	    echo "ios-check: FAIL — pbxproj does not link AppIcon.icon into the Resources phase ${REINIT_HINT}" >&2
201	    fail=1
202	  fi
203	fi
204	
205	# Structural guard: a sentinel-present-but-corrupt pbxproj must still fail the check.
206	if command -v plutil >/dev/null 2>&1 && ! plutil -lint "${PBXPROJ}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
207	  echo "ios-check: FAIL — project.pbxproj does not parse (plutil -lint)" >&2
208	  fail=1
209	fi
210	
211	if [ "${fail}" -ne 0 ]; then
212	  exit 1
213	fi
214	echo "ios-check: OK — template-rendered project carries every workaround"
215

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# ios-template-check.sh — keep the forked XcodeGen template in lockstep with the
3	# pinned tauri-cli. Linux-runnable; part of `just ci` / `just ci-pds`.
4	#
5	# scripts/ios/project.yml is a fork of tauri-cli's built-in iOS project template
6	# (rendered into gen/apple/project.yml on every `cargo tauri ios init` via
7	# `bundle > iOS > template`). Replacing upstream's template wholesale means upstream
8	# changes to it — new build settings, search-path fixes — no longer reach us
9	# automatically. This gate closes that hole at the only moment drift can enter:
10	# when someone bumps the tauri-cli pin in the workflows without re-merging the
11	# upstream template, the versions disagree and CI fails with instructions.
12	#
13	# It also asserts the structural invariants the macOS-side ios-check verifies in
14	# the *generated* project — here checked in the *source* template, so a Linux PR
15	# that breaks the template fails before it ever reaches the macOS lanes.
16	set -euo pipefail
17	
18	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
19	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "${SCRIPT_DIR}/.." && pwd)"
20	TEMPLATE="${REPO_ROOT}/scripts/ios/project.yml"
21	PRISTINE="${REPO_ROOT}/scripts/ios/upstream-project.yml"
22	
23	fail=0
24	
25	if [ ! -f "${TEMPLATE}" ]; then
26	  echo "ios-template-check: FAIL — ${TEMPLATE} missing" >&2
27	  exit 1
28	fi
29	if [ ! -f "${PRISTINE}" ]; then
30	  echo "ios-template-check: FAIL — ${PRISTINE} missing (the pristine upstream copy used to diff the fork)" >&2
31	  fail=1
32	fi
33	
34	# --- Version lockstep: template stamp == every workflow's tauri-cli pin ---
35	stamped="$(sed -n 's/^# upstream-version: tauri-cli \([0-9][0-9.]*\)$/\1/p' "${TEMPLATE}")"
36	if [ -z "${stamped}" ]; then
37	  echo "ios-template-check: FAIL — no '# upstream-version: tauri-cli X.Y.Z' line in ${TEMPLATE}" >&2
38	  fail=1
39	else
40	  pins_found=0
41	  # The tauri-cli pin now lives in the shared runner-preamble composite action
42	  # (.github/actions/ios-setup/action.yml) — one home for all iOS lanes. Scan it
43	  # alongside the workflow files so a pin lingering in either location is still caught.
44	  for wf in "${REPO_ROOT}"/.github/workflows/*.yml "${REPO_ROOT}"/.github/actions/ios-setup/action.yml; do
45	    [ -f "${wf}" ] || continue
46	    pin="$(sed -n "s/.*cargo binstall -y --locked tauri-cli --version '\([0-9][0-9.]*\)'.*/\1/p" "${wf}")"
47	    [ -z "${pin}" ] && continue
48	    pins_found=$((pins_found + 1))
49	    if [ "${pin}" != "${stamped}" ]; then
50	      echo "ios-template-check: FAIL — $(basename "${wf}") pins tauri-cli ${pin}, but scripts/ios/project.yml is forked from ${stamped}." >&2
51	      echo "  To bump: fetch the new tag's crates/tauri-cli/templates/mobile/ios/project.yml into" >&2
52	      echo "  scripts/ios/upstream-project.yml, re-merge upstream's changes into scripts/ios/project.yml" >&2
53	      echo "  (the ezpds changes are marked with 'ezpds:' comments), and update its upstream-version line." >&2
54	      fail=1
55	    fi
56	  done
57	  if [ "${pins_found}" -eq 0 ]; then
58	    echo "ios-template-check: FAIL — no tauri-cli binstall pin found in .github/workflows/*.yml or .github/actions/ios-setup/action.yml (did the pin format or location change? update this script's sed)" >&2
59	    fail=1
60	  fi
61	fi
62	
63	# --- Structural invariants of the fork (source-side mirror of ios-check.sh) ---
64	require() {
65	  local pattern="$1" why="$2"
66	  # -F: the "patterns" are literal template text full of regex metacharacters
67	  # ($(inherited), {{#each ...}}) — fixed-string matching keeps a future edit
68	  # from accidentally forming a valid regex with different semantics.
69	  if ! grep -qF -- "${pattern}" "${TEMPLATE}"; then
70	    echo "ios-template-check: FAIL — template lost '${pattern}' (${why})" >&2
71	    fail=1
72	  fi
73	}
74	require 'ezpds-ios-template' "the sentinel ios-check greps in the rendered project.yml"
75	require 'ENABLE_USER_SCRIPT_SANDBOXING: "NO"' "macOS 26 Run Script sandbox blocks Cargo (Bug 2)"
76	require 'CODE_SIGN_ALLOW_ENTITLEMENTS_MODIFICATION: "YES"' "spurious entitlements-modified failure (Bug 3)"
77	require 'OTHER_LDFLAGS: $(inherited){{#each ios-frameworks}} -framework {{this}}{{/each}}' "staticlib framework linking from bundle > iOS > frameworks"
78	require '# >>> ezpds-ios-env >>>' "dev-env preamble in the Build Rust Code phase"
79	if ! grep -A1 -E '^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*path:[[:space:]]*Externals[[:space:]]*$' "${TEMPLATE}" | grep -q 'buildPhase: none'; then
80	  echo "ios-template-check: FAIL — template's Externals source lost 'buildPhase: none' (libapp.a would be bundled; tauri#13578)" >&2
81	  fail=1
82	fi
83	require '- path: ../../../AppIcon.icon' "the layered Icon Composer document (iOS 26 Liquid Glass icon), referenced in place"
84	# The fileTypes mapping must keep .icon packages single-file (XcodeGen#1556 —
85	# without it the package is exploded into loose resources Xcode won't use).
86	if ! grep -A2 -E '^[[:space:]]*fileTypes:' "${TEMPLATE}" | grep -q 'icon:'; then
87	  echo "ios-template-check: FAIL — template lost the fileTypes .icon=file mapping (XcodeGen would explode the AppIcon.icon package; XcodeGen#1556)" >&2
88	  fail=1
89	fi
90	# Both apps must actually ship the document the template references for every app.
91	for app in identity-wallet admin-companion; do
92	  if [ ! -f "${REPO_ROOT}/apps/${app}/AppIcon.icon/icon.json" ]; then
93	    echo "ios-template-check: FAIL — apps/${app}/AppIcon.icon/icon.json missing (the template references ../../../AppIcon.icon for every app)" >&2
94	    fail=1
95	  fi
96	done
97	
98	# --- Entitlements: tauri's default path in the template, content via Patch H ---
99	# The template MUST keep tauri-cli's default entitlements path: tauri's build-time
100	# codesign reads that exact path regardless of the template, so a repoint leaves it
101	# fileless and signing dies with "cannot read entitlement data". The tracked per-app
102	# src-tauri/Entitlements.ios.plist is the source of truth; ios-postinit's Patch H
103	# copies it into the generated default file (verified by ios-check's sha marker).
104	require 'path: {{app.name}}_iOS/{{app.name}}_iOS.entitlements' "tauri's default entitlements path (do NOT repoint — breaks build-time codesign)"
105	for app in identity-wallet admin-companion; do
106	  if [ ! -f "${REPO_ROOT}/apps/${app}/src-tauri/Entitlements.ios.plist" ]; then
107	    echo "ios-template-check: FAIL — apps/${app}/src-tauri/Entitlements.ios.plist missing (Patch H installs it into every app's generated project)" >&2
108	    fail=1
109	  fi
110	done
111	# The wallet's blob backup needs the iCloud ubiquity container; the container id
112	# must also be declared to the Files app in Info.ios.plist (NSUbiquitousContainers).
113	WALLET_ENT="${REPO_ROOT}/apps/identity-wallet/src-tauri/Entitlements.ios.plist"
114	WALLET_CONTAINER='iCloud.dev.malpercio.identitywallet'
115	if [ -f "${WALLET_ENT}" ]; then
116	  # The container is matched in its <string> form: the file's explanatory comments quote the
117	  # bare id, so a plain substring match would be satisfied by prose alone and keep passing after
118	  # the real entitlement was deleted. `just bundle-identity-check` validates the same contract
119	  # against the parsed nodes.
120	  for key in 'com.apple.developer.ubiquity-container-identifiers' 'com.apple.developer.icloud-services' "<string>${WALLET_CONTAINER}</string>"; do
121	    if ! grep -qF -- "${key}" "${WALLET_ENT}"; then
122	      echo "ios-template-check: FAIL — wallet Entitlements.ios.plist lost '${key}' (the iCloud Drive blob backup mirror needs it)" >&2
123	      fail=1
124	    fi
125	  done
126	fi
127	if ! grep -qF -- "${WALLET_CONTAINER}" "${REPO_ROOT}/apps/identity-wallet/src-tauri/Info.ios.plist"; then
128	  echo "ios-template-check: FAIL — wallet Info.ios.plist lost the NSUbiquitousContainers entry for ${WALLET_CONTAINER} (the backup mirror would be invisible in the Files app)" >&2
129	  fail=1
130	fi
131	# Least privilege: the operator console must NOT grow iCloud entitlements — only
132	# the wallet's blob backup is entitled to a ubiquity container. Case-insensitive,
133	# and 'ubiquity' included: the ubiquity-container key has no "icloud" substring,
134	# and container values are conventionally capitalized ("iCloud.…").
135	if grep -qiE 'icloud|ubiquity' "${REPO_ROOT}/apps/admin-companion/src-tauri/Entitlements.ios.plist"; then
136	  echo "ios-template-check: FAIL — admin-companion Entitlements.ios.plist declares an iCloud entitlement (least privilege: only the wallet's blob backup needs one)" >&2
137	  fail=1
138	fi
139	
140	# --- Both apps must actually point at the template ---
141	for app in identity-wallet admin-companion; do
142	  conf="${REPO_ROOT}/apps/${app}/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json"
143	  if ! grep -q '"template": "../../scripts/ios/project.yml"' "${conf}"; then
144	    echo "ios-template-check: FAIL — ${conf} does not set bundle > iOS > template to ../../scripts/ios/project.yml" >&2
145	    fail=1
146	  fi
147	done
148	
149	if [ "${fail}" -ne 0 ]; then
150	  exit 1
151	fi
152	echo "ios-template-check: OK — template in lockstep with tauri-cli ${stamped}"
153

118	  The `aps.alert` text is a generic placeholder — Apple never sees plaintext either.
119	
120	### 4. Receiving (NSE decrypts on the fly)
121	
122	- `mutable-content: 1` routes the push through the app's **Notification Service
123	  Extension**. The NSE loads the notification private key and the pinned sender public key
124	  from the shared keychain, HPKE-opens the payload, verifies origin, and replaces the
125	  placeholder title/body with the decrypted content before the banner is shown. This is
126	  exactly "the app decrypts payloads on the fly."
127	- **Failure handling** — an important iOS constraint frames this: an NSE **cannot
128	  suppress** an alert push. If the extension fails, times out, or declines to attach
129	  content, iOS displays the original payload (our generic placeholder) anyway. So
130	  "suppress invalid payloads" is not on the menu; the design instead controls *what*
131	  surfaces. A payload that fails decryption or origin verification is rendered as an
132	  explicitly-marked **unverified** generic notice ("Couldn't verify a notification from
133	  your Custos instance") — never as authentic-looking content — and the app records a
134	  local diagnostic surfaced in-app so repeated failures (key desync, misbehaving relay)
135	  are visible and debuggable rather than mysterious.
136	
137	## Trust model
138	
139	What the relay **can** do (and what we accept):
140	- Deliver, drop, delay, or reorder notifications — it is trusted for **availability only**.
141	- Observe metadata: sender node id, target push handle/APNs token, timing, frequency, and
142	  padded size. Padding buckets + no persistent per-send logs (beyond rate-limit counters)
143	  keep this to the minimum APNs itself already observes.
144	
145	What the relay **cannot** do:
146	- Read content — HPKE-sealed to the device key; the relay holds no decryption key.
147	- Forge or alter **authenticated content** — HPKE **Auth mode** binds the ciphertext to
148	  the instance's pinned sender key, so nothing the relay fabricates or modifies ever
149	  renders as content from the user's Custos. Two honest qualifications:
150	  - **It can still generate noise.** The relay holds the APNs key, so it can always send
151	    junk pushes (with or without our envelope), and iOS will not let the NSE suppress
152	    them — they surface as the explicitly-marked unverified notice, never as authentic
153	    content. That is detectable spam and grounds for switching relays, not impersonation.
154	  - **It can replay.** HPKE adds no anti-replay guarantee, so a captured sealed payload
155	    can be redelivered. v1 explicitly accepts duplicate authenticated notifications as
156	    benign (a repeated banner, no state change — notifications drive no writes); a
157	    per-device monotonic counter inside the sealed payload is the upgrade path if that
158	    stops being acceptable (see Open questions).
159	- Correlate handles to identities — Custos never sends DIDs, handles, or account data to
160	  the relay.
161	
162	A compromised **Custos instance** can read/forge its own users' notifications — but the
163	instance is the operator's own trust root already; nothing new is ceded.
164	
165	**Metadata-minimizing mode (optional, per user or per instance):** send a content-free
166	`content-available` ping instead of a sealed payload; the app fetches the actual events from
167	its Custos over HTTPS/iroh on wake. Maximum privacy (the relay sees only "something
168	happened"), but iOS aggressively throttles background pushes, so visible-alert quality
169	suffers. Offering both modes lets users pick their point on the privacy/UX curve; the sealed
170	payload is the default.
171	
172	## Sovereignty and openness

result.output:
# --- iOS lanes (identity-wallet + admin-companion) --------------------------------
# Imported by the root justfile. Run from the repo root; requires macOS + Xcode.
# The two apps share one toolchain seam: the per-app scripts under
# apps/<app>/scripts/ are thin wrappers over the ONE shared implementation in
# scripts/ios/. The public per-app recipes here are likewise thin delegates over
# private parameterized recipes (`_dev`, `_build`, `_pr-check`, `_upload`, `_ipa`,
# `_icon-compile`), so an identity-wallet ⇄ admin-companion pair can't drift.
#
# Both build recipes `export EZPDS_IOS_BUILD=1 && . scripts/ios-env.sh` before
# `cargo tauri` so the OUTER process re-resolves the Apple toolchain, overriding any
# stale CARGO_TARGET_*/CC_*/AR_* a long-lived dev shell may carry from a pre-fix
# ios-env.sh sourcing (see apps/identity-wallet/AGENTS.md "Development Workflow").

# --- Shared private recipes (parameterized over the app) ---

# Launch an app on the iOS Simulator. With no device, `cargo tauri ios dev`
# auto-selects a target and PREFERS a connected physical device (which needs code
# signing); pass a simulator name to force the Simulator even with a device plugged in.
_dev app_dir device:
    cd {{app_dir}} && export EZPDS_IOS_BUILD=1 && . scripts/ios-env.sh && if [ -n "{{device}}" ]; then cargo tauri ios dev "{{device}}"; else cargo tauri ios dev; fi

# Build an app for the Simulator.
_build app_dir:
    cd {{app_dir}} && export EZPDS_IOS_BUILD=1 && . scripts/ios-env.sh && cargo tauri ios build --debug

# PR-time iOS gate body (no signing, no secrets, no xcodebuild archive): build the
# frontend (tauri's codegen embeds ../dist at compile time), cross-compile the app's
# staticlib for the iOS device target, then run the app's Rust unit tests and clippy on
# the macOS host target (the only CI lane that can compile these crates — the Linux
# ci-pds gate excludes them, so without the clippy step here nothing gates lints for
# these two crates and findings silently accumulate). The host test/clippy runs
# deliberately do NOT set EZPDS_IOS_BUILD (that would clobber CC/AR with iOS toolchain
# overrides). The `<app>-check` +
# `_icon-compile` dependencies (which exercise the whole Apple/Rust seam) are declared
# on the public delegates so each app runs its own check.
_pr-check app_dir crate:
    cd {{app_dir}} && pnpm build
    cd {{app_dir}} && export EZPDS_IOS_BUILD=1 && . scripts/ios-env.sh && cargo build --locked --lib --target aarch64-apple-ios -p {{crate}}
    cargo test --locked -p {{crate}}
    cargo clippy --locked -p {{crate}} --all-targets -- -D warnings

# Upload the most recently built IPA to App Store Connect / TestFlight via altool.
# Requires APPLE_API_KEY (key id) + APPLE_API_ISSUER (issuer id) in the environment
# and the matching AuthKey_<key id>.p8 in ~/.appstoreconnect/private_keys/.
_upload app_dir ipa_recipe:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    # Newest .ipa by mtime — `ls -t` picks the freshest build, not the alphabetically
    # first (which could be a stale pre-rename artifact). `|| true` tolerates no match.
    ipa="$(ls -t {{app_dir}}/src-tauri/gen/apple/build/arm64/*.ipa 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)"
    if [ -z "$ipa" ]; then
      echo "no .ipa found - run 'just {{ipa_recipe}}' first" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "uploading $ipa to TestFlight..."
    xcrun altool --upload-app --type ios --file "$ipa" --apiKey "$APPLE_API_KEY" --apiIssuer "$APPLE_API_ISSUER"

# --- iOS release signing (shared by both apps) ---
# CI runs the release recipes on a GitHub macOS runner (.github/workflows/
# ios-testflight.yml, admin-testflight.yml); they double as the local
# `just ios-release`/`admin-release` escape hatch.
# SIGNING is explicit (Tauri's automatic iOS signing is unreliable — it emits an
# "Apple Distribution: Tauri (unset)" placeholder that App Store Connect rejects):
#   IOS_CERTIFICATE (base64 .p12) + IOS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD + IOS_MOBILE_PROVISION
#   (base64 App Store .mobileprovision; admin-companion uses its own bundle-id-bound
#   profile, IOS_MOBILE_PROVISION_ADMIN, in its workflow).
# UPLOAD uses the App Store Connect API key: APPLE_API_KEY + APPLE_API_ISSUER and the
# matching AuthKey_<id>.p8 in ~/.appstoreconnect/private_keys/. See docs/ios-cicd.md.

# Shared implementation behind `ios-ipa`/`admin-ipa`: stamp a unique, monotonic
# CFBundleVersion into the app's tauri.conf.json, build the signed App Store IPA, and
# restore the config afterwards.
#
# BUILD NUMBER: TestFlight rejects duplicate CFBundleVersions and requires them to
# increase, so CI and the local escape hatch must share ONE stamping scheme — stamping
# only in the workflow (the old design) made a second local `just ios-release` collide
# on the committed placeholder value. Default is UTC epoch seconds: unique, strictly
# increasing across CI and local runs alike, immune to the reset a workflow-file rename
# inflicts on GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER, and larger than any run number already uploaded (so
# the changeover is monotonic).
#
# RESTORE is `git checkout` of the committed file, not a backup copy: a SIGKILL skips
# the EXIT trap, and with a copy-based restore the next run would back up the
# already-stamped file as its new "original", losing the committed value for good.
# Because the git restore discards local edits to the file, the guard refuses to run
# while tauri.conf.json has uncommitted changes.
_ipa app_dir build_number:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    # Drop any stale .ipa first (e.g. a pre-rename artifact) so the upload recipes can't pick it up.
    rm -f {{app_dir}}/src-tauri/gen/apple/build/arm64/*.ipa
    conf="$(pwd)/{{app_dir}}/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json"
    if ! git diff --quiet -- "$conf"; then
      echo "✗ $conf has uncommitted changes — commit or stash them first" >&2
      echo "  (the post-build restore is 'git checkout -- <conf>', which would discard them)" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    bv="{{build_number}}"
    [ -n "$bv" ] || bv="$(date -u +%s)"
    trap 'git checkout -- "$conf"' EXIT
    tmp="$(mktemp)"
    jq --arg bv "$bv" '.bundle.iOS.bundleVersion = $bv' "$conf" > "$tmp" && mv "$tmp" "$conf"
    echo "CFBundleVersion -> $bv"
    cd {{app_dir}} && export EZPDS_IOS_BUILD=1 && . scripts/ios-env.sh
    # SwiftPM manifest compilation for the vendored swift-rs fork occasionally crashes the
    # Apple toolchain non-deterministically: `clang` dies with `Segmentation fault: 11`
    # while linking the throwaway Package.swift manifest executable, panicking swift-rs's
    # build script ("Failed to compile swift package Tauri") and failing the whole lane.
    # It is a transient toolchain crash, not a build defect — the identical build passes on
    # retry and passed on the sibling app's lane for the same commit. Retry ONLY that
    # signature (a clang crash-by-signal); any other failure — a real Rust/Swift compile
    # error or a signing failure — still fails fast on the first attempt.
    # See docs/ios-upstream-bugs.md Bug 4.
    transient_re='Segmentation fault: 11|linker command failed due to signal|unable to execute command: (Segmentation fault|Killed)'
    attempts=3
    for attempt in $(seq 1 "$attempts"); do
      buildlog="$(mktemp)"
      if cargo tauri ios build --export-method app-store-connect 2>&1 | tee "$buildlog"; then
        rm -f "$buildlog"
        exit 0
      fi
      status="${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
      if [ "$attempt" -lt "$attempts" ] && grep -qE "$transient_re" "$buildlog"; then
        echo "⚠ transient Apple-toolchain crash during swift-rs manifest compile (attempt $attempt/$attempts) — retrying" >&2
        rm -f "$buildlog"
        continue
      fi
      rm -f "$buildlog"
      exit "$status"
    done

# Compile the app's Icon Composer document (AppIcon.icon, referenced in place by
# the scripts/ios/project.yml template) with actool — the same compiler Xcode's
# build invokes — so a malformed icon.json or a layer SVG the Apple toolchain
# can't parse fails the PR gate instead of the post-merge TestFlight archive.
# macOS-only (xcrun); the callers are the macOS pr-check recipes. actool's exit
# code alone is not trustworthy, so the recipe also requires an Assets.car and
# greps the tool output for errors. A MISSING bundle fails too: both apps ship
# one, so absence in this gate means a miswired path, not an icon-less app.
_icon-compile app_dir:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    icon="{{app_dir}}/AppIcon.icon"
    if [ ! -d "$icon" ]; then
      echo "✗ missing AppIcon.icon in {{app_dir}} — both apps ship one; a missing bundle here means a miswired path" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    out="$(mktemp -d)"
    log="$(xcrun actool "$icon" --compile "$out" \
      --platform iphoneos --minimum-deployment-target 14.0 \
      --app-icon AppIcon --output-partial-info-plist "$out/AppIcon-partial.plist" \
      --output-format human-readable-text --notices --warnings 2>&1)" || { echo "$log" >&2; exit 1; }
    echo "$log"
    if echo "$log" | grep -qi ': error:'; then
      echo "✗ actool reported errors compiling $icon" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    if [ ! -f "$out/Assets.car" ]; then
      echo "✗ actool produced no Assets.car from $icon" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "✓ actool compiled $icon"

# --- identity-wallet (Obsign) ---

# Finish setting up the generated Xcode project (swift-rs fork check + app icon), then
# verify it. The Xcode-project workarounds themselves come from the committed template
# scripts/ios/project.yml, rendered on every `cargo tauri ios init`. Run once after
# every init. Idempotent.
ios-postinit:
    apps/identity-wallet/scripts/ios-postinit.sh

# Fail if the generated Xcode project is missing any required workaround (i.e. the
# scripts/ios/project.yml template did not apply, or gen/apple predates it).
ios-check:
    apps/identity-wallet/scripts/ios-check.sh

# Launch the app on the iOS Simulator (verifies patches first). Pass a simulator name
# to force the Simulator even while a device is plugged in, e.g.
# `just ios-dev "iPhone 17 Pro Max"`.
ios-dev device="": ios-check
    just _dev apps/identity-wallet "{{device}}"

# Build the iOS app for the Simulator (verifies patches first).
ios-build: ios-check
    just _build apps/identity-wallet

# PR-time iOS gate (.github/workflows/ios-pr-check.yml) — no signing, no secrets, no
# xcodebuild archive. See `_pr-check`. Via the ios-check + _icon-compile dependencies
# this exercises the whole Apple/Rust seam a PR can break: the scripts/ios/project.yml
# template rendering, the swift-rs fork (vendored plugin Swift compilation), and the
# shared workspace crates on aarch64-apple-ios.
# Assumes the Xcode project exists: run `cargo tauri ios init` + `just ios-postinit` first.
ios-pr-check: ios-check (_icon-compile "apps/identity-wallet")
    just _pr-check apps/identity-wallet identity-wallet

# Build a signed, App Store-method IPA (for TestFlight or the App Store). Assumes the
# Xcode project exists: run `cargo tauri ios init` + `just ios-postinit` once first
# (CI does both every run). NOTE: the --export-method token tracks Xcode's names
# (`app-store-connect` on Xcode 15+); confirm once with `cargo tauri ios build --help`.
# Build-number stamping: see `_ipa`. Override the default: `just ios-ipa 12345`.
ios-ipa build_number="": ios-check
    just _ipa apps/identity-wallet "{{build_number}}"

# Upload the most recently built identity-wallet IPA to TestFlight. See `_upload`.
ios-upload:
    just _upload apps/identity-wallet ios-ipa

# Full local release lane: build the signed IPA, then upload to TestFlight.
ios-release: ios-ipa ios-upload

# --- admin-companion (the operator console, "Brass Console") ---
# A second iOS app. Same toolchain seam as identity-wallet; the scripts are
# path-relative so they patch this app's own generated Xcode project. Its App Store
# profile is bound to admin-companion's own bundle id (dev.malpercio.admincompanion) —
# see docs/ios-cicd.md.

# Finish setting up admin-companion's generated Xcode project (swift-rs fork check +
# app icon), then verify it — the workarounds come from the scripts/ios/project.yml
# template. Run once after every `cargo tauri ios init`. Idempotent.
admin-postinit:
    apps/admin-companion/scripts/ios-postinit.sh

# Fail if admin-companion's generated Xcode project is missing any required workaround
# (i.e. the scripts/ios/project.yml template did not apply, or gen/apple predates it).
admin-check:
    apps/admin-companion/scripts/ios-check.sh

# Launch the admin console on the iOS Simulator (verifies patches first).
# Pass a simulator name to force the Simulator, e.g. `just admin-dev "iPhone 17 Pro Max"`.
admin-dev device="": admin-check
    just _dev apps/admin-companion "{{device}}"

# Build the admin console for the Simulator (verifies patches first).
admin-build: admin-check
    just _build apps/admin-companion

# PR-time iOS gate for the admin console — same shape as `just ios-pr-check`. See `_pr-check`.
# Assumes the Xcode project exists: `cargo tauri ios init` + `just admin-postinit` first.
admin-pr-check: admin-check (_icon-compile "apps/admin-companion")
    just _pr-check apps/admin-companion admin-companion

# Build a signed, App Store-method IPA for the admin console. Assumes the Xcode
# project exists: run `cargo tauri ios init` + `just admin-postinit` once first
# (CI does both every run). Build-number stamping: see `_ipa`; override:
# `just admin-ipa 12345`.
admin-ipa build_number="": admin-check
    just _ipa apps/admin-companion "{{build_number}}"

# Upload the most recently built admin-companion IPA to TestFlight. See `_upload`.
admin-upload:
    just _upload apps/admin-companion admin-ipa

# Full local release lane: build the signed IPA, then upload to TestFlight.
admin-release: admin-ipa admin-upload

257	## Push notifications: three artifacts, often confused
258	
259	"Set up APNs" collapses three separate things that live in different places and fail in
260	different ways. Keeping them apart is what makes a broken push diagnosable.
261	
262	**1. The app's `aps-environment` entitlement** (shipped). Enabled on the App ID and carried
263	in the wallet's tracked entitlements; it is what makes `registerForRemoteNotifications`
264	return a device token. Missing it means the app never obtains a token at all — the wallet
265	reports `AWAITING_APNS_TOKEN` forever and registers with no server, which reads as "nothing
266	happens" rather than as an error. This is the only one of the three that gates the wallet's
267	own build, via the profile-regeneration rule in [step 3](#2-app-store-connect) above.
268	
269	**2. The Notification Service Extension's App ID** (with the extension itself). An app
270	extension is a **separate bundle** (`dev.malpercio.identitywallet.<name>`), so it needs its
271	own explicit App ID, its own distribution profile signed by the same team cert, and its own
272	`IOS_MOBILE_PROVISION_*`-style secret — the same three-artifact shape the Admin Companion
273	lane above already establishes. It does **not** need `aps-environment` (that is an app
274	entitlement, not an extension one); what it needs is the shared keychain access group, which
275	needs no portal work for the reason given in step 3.
276	
277	**3. The relay's APNs auth key** (not an app artifact at all). Certificates, Identifiers &
278	Profiles → **Keys** → a new key with **Apple Push Notifications service (APNs)** enabled,
279	downloadable exactly once. It configures `crates/notify-relay`, not either app:
280	
281	| Relay config | Env | What it is |
282	|---|---|---|
283	| `apns.key_path` | `EZPDS_NOTIFY_APNS_KEY_PATH` | the `.p8` file |
284	| `apns.key_id` | `EZPDS_NOTIFY_APNS_KEY_ID` | the key's identifier (the JWT `kid`) |
285	| `apns.team_id` | `EZPDS_NOTIFY_APNS_TEAM_ID` | the 10-character Team ID |
286	| `apns.topics` | `EZPDS_NOTIFY_APNS_TOPICS` | the bundle ids this relay serves |
287	
288	Config validation requires the first three together, and the relay refuses to register a
289	handle whose topic is outside `apns.topics`. This key is the structural reason the relay
290	exists: an APNs key is team-bound, so a self-hoster cannot push to the official bundle ids
291	and must route through a relay that holds it — see
292	[the notification relay design](design-plans/2026-07-10-notification-relay.md).
